title: fix(ui): keep Gateway downtime visible without losing drafts
body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191925

The Control UI now opens its normal shell while the Gateway starts or reconnects. Existing conversations retain their shell and draft; genuine authentication failures still use sign-in. Navigation becomes available with the connection, and manual recovery appears after automatic recovery stops.

Available app documents and static assets remain usable during startup and drain. Dynamic requests, OAuth callbacks, and proxy attribution retain their existing owners. When the app document is unavailable, an asset-free page retries the same URL automatically, including when a previously resolved UI directory loses its index. The approved desktop/mobile layout and designer wordmarks are retained.

Validation on Tempbook after integrating main:

- Corrected three Gateway lineage expectations attributable to this PR: automatic non-auth retries keep the shell; credential re-scoping and manual connection fixtures now enter a terminal login state. All 11 existing lineage cases pass (5.57 s wall with `pnpm test ui/src/app/app-host.gateway-lineage.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`), as do targeted oxlint/format and UI-app test types (8.45 s). Credential/owner boundaries and existing authentication and warm-boot coverage are unchanged. This follow-up changes only the test file; no new build or broad suite was run.

- Retained both serial browser-test entries in the sole merge conflict. The three inventory cases pass (9.82 s). The 31 connection/warm-boot UI cases pass (4.51 s), and all seven startup HTTP cases pass (36.93 s), including OAuth ownership and missing-index/root recovery.
- Removed an unsupported decorative SVG attribute and expanded the reduced-motion selectors without changing specificity or appearance. Both original type/lint failures are resolved; the 13 connection cases pass again (3.19 s). UI/core/tooling types and focused lint/stylelint/format checks pass. The test allocation remains 1328 lines, with no scalar increase or new tests; test-line and source-line caps pass.
- Earlier proof at `e31662b19c4` is retained for unchanged paths: 100 HTTP/routing, 10 browser, and three isolated real-Gateway cases, including actual SIGUSR2/socket reconnection with shell, URL, and draft retention. Those results and the full independent source review are historical evidence, not current-head CI. The two HTTP findings from that review were reproduced and fixed. This integration needed no new behavior or design decision and no repeated full review or E2E suite.

The merge preserves main's ingress/runtime changes, `InlineAlert` standardization, and sidebar behavior, plus all four collaborator branding commits. The production UI build passes. Authorized asset-budget overruns: startup JS gzip +206 B, largest JS gzip +3,316 B, total CSS gzip +936 B/raw +2,648 B, chat boot JS gzip +4,173 B, and new-session boot JS gzip +4,495 B. Hosted CI remains pending; no full UI/E2E suite, full generated-locale parity, binary upgrade, or host reboot was run. Earlier CI's unchanged lazy `chat.sessionSharing.share` expectation and startup-only logs are not claimed fixed. Local times use `pnpm test … --maxWorkers=1`; hosted CI seconds are not yet available.

The connection view centers its title and line under the OpenClaw mascot, whose slow bob, claws and eye scan are the busy indicator; the phone header, right above it, shows only the text wordmark, while the sidebar keeps the full lockup. The captures use the source UI with a held mock Gateway connection at desktop/mobile widths and reduced motion, so the mascot rests on its ground. Main has no held-connection view under the same mock, so they are after-only.
